# RoundsVaultBase
[Git Source](https://github.com/OasisDEX/summer-earn-protocol/blob/main/packages/core-contracts/src/contracts/rounds-vault/RoundsVaultBase.sol)

**Inherits:**
ProtocolAccessManagedV2, [ERC4626MultiTokenWrapper](../../extensions/erc4626-multi-token-wrapper.md), [Whitelist](../../utils/Whitelist/whitelist.md), [IRoundsVaultBase](../../interfaces/rounds-vault/i-rounds-vault-base.md), [IRoundsVaultBaseErrors](../../interfaces/rounds-vault/i-rounds-vault-base-errors.md), [IRoundsVaultBaseEvents](../../interfaces/rounds-vault/i-rounds-vault-base-events.md), [IRoundsVaultBaseEnums](../../interfaces/rounds-vault/i-rounds-vault-base-enums.md)

**Title:**
RoundsVaultBase

**Author:**
Roberto Cano <robercano>

Abstract base that batches user activity into discrete rounds and only moves funds in or
out of a target ERC-4626 vault when the keeper closes and settles each round. Lets users
interact at any block even when the target vault settles asynchronously (e.g. T+0/T+1
against an off-chain NAV strike).

Public ABI is described by `IRoundsVaultBase`. Concrete subclasses (`RoundsVaultInput` and
`RoundsVaultOutput`) pick a `BaseVaultType` at construction and implement the two virtual
hooks `_operate` (the settlement trade) and `_getFallbackExchangeRate` (the rate used when
a round was empty). Typical `_operate` implementations call `_depositOnTarget` or
`_redeemFromTarget` to move funds in or out of the target vault.

Access control: round-state transitions (`nextRound`, `setRoundSettled[Batch]`, `retryRound`)
are keeper-gated; `emergencyRollbackRound` and `setMinPositionSize` are governor-gated. User
flows (`deposit`, `redeem[Batch]`, `redeemExchangeAsset[Batch]`, ERC-1155 transfers) require
every involved party (caller/owner/receiver) to be whitelisted on the target vault context.


## State Variables
### _roundNumber
STORAGE

The currently open round number; starts at 0 and is incremented by `nextRound`.


```solidity
uint256 private _roundNumber
```


### _exchangeRateByRound
Per-round settlement exchange rate, snapshotted by `_setRoundSettled`.

Rounds that have not been settled read back the zero-valued `Price`.


```solidity
mapping(uint256 => Price) private _exchangeRateByRound
```


### _exchangeAsset
The ERC-20 token paid out when exchanging a settled-round receipt.

For an Input vault this is the target vault's share token; for an Output vault this is
the target vault's underlying asset.


```solidity
address private _exchangeAsset
```


### roundState
Lifecycle state of each round id (see `IRoundsVaultBaseEnums.RoundState`).

Default value `NotOpened` for any id the contract has never written. The constructor
seeds `roundState[0] = Opened` so round 0 is usable from deployment.


```solidity
mapping(uint256 => RoundState) public roundState
```


### minPositionSize
Minimum aggregate position size, in target-vault assets, that a user must maintain
to enter or exit. `0` disables the check.


```solidity
uint256 public minPositionSize
```


### VAULT_TYPE
Vault flavor configured at construction. Determines the deposit and exchange assets.

`Input`:  deposit asset = proxiedVault.asset(), exchange asset = proxiedVault (shares).
`Output`: deposit asset = proxiedVault (shares), exchange asset = proxiedVault.asset().


```solidity
BaseVaultType public immutable VAULT_TYPE
```


## Functions
### constructor

CONSTRUCTOR

Wires the rounds-vault to a target ERC-4626 vault and the protocol access manager.

Opens round 0 (`roundState[0] = Opened`) so the contract is usable immediately after
deployment. Assumes the target ERC-4626 vault uses itself as its own share token, per
the OpenZeppelin reference implementation.


```solidity
constructor(
    address proxiedERC4626Vault,
    BaseVaultType _vaultType,
    address accessManager,
    string memory receiptsURI
)
    ERC4626MultiTokenWrapper(
        proxiedERC4626Vault,
        _vaultType == BaseVaultType.Input ? IERC4626(proxiedERC4626Vault).asset() : proxiedERC4626Vault,
        receiptsURI
    )
    ProtocolAccessManagedV2(accessManager);
```
**Parameters**

|Name|Type|Description|
|----|----|-----------|
|`proxiedERC4626Vault`|`address`|The target ERC-4626 vault this rounds-vault wraps. Funds move in and out of it once per round, via `_operate`.|
|`_vaultType`|`BaseVaultType`|The vault flavor (`Input` or `Output`). Determines the deposit/exchange asset pair: - `Input`:  deposit asset = `proxiedERC4626Vault.asset()`, exchange asset = `proxiedERC4626Vault` (its shares); - `Output`: deposit asset = `proxiedERC4626Vault` (its shares), exchange asset = `proxiedERC4626Vault.asset()`.|
|`accessManager`|`address`|The `ProtocolAccessManagerV2` instance that brokers Keeper/Governor roles and the whitelist. The Keeper role is required for `nextRound`, `setRoundSettled[Batch]` and `retryRound`; the Governor role is required for `emergencyRollbackRound` and `setMinPositionSize`.|
|`receiptsURI`|`string`|The ERC-1155 metadata URI for round receipts minted on deposit.|


### nextRound

PUBLIC FUNCTIONS

No funds move here; settlement is a separate keeper call (`setRoundSettled`). Reverts if
the current round is not in `Opened` state. Restricted to the keeper role.


```solidity
function nextRound() external onlyKeeper;
```

### retryRound

Pushes a past round in `Opened` state back to `InSettlement` so the keeper can attempt
settlement again.

Only valid for past rounds (`roundId < currentRound`) that are in `Opened` state. The
typical recovery sequence is `emergencyRollbackRound` then `retryRound` then
`setRoundSettled`. Reverts on the current round or on rounds in any other state.
Restricted to the keeper role.


```solidity
function retryRound(uint256 roundId) external onlyKeeper;
```
**Parameters**

|Name|Type|Description|
|----|----|-----------|
|`roundId`|`uint256`|The id of the round to retry|


### setRoundSettled

Executes the settlement trade for a round that is currently in `InSettlement` and
snapshots the per-round exchange rate from the actual trade result.

Marks the round as `Settled` before calling `_operate`, so any reentrant attempt to
re-settle the same round reverts on state. Restricted to the keeper role.


```solidity
function setRoundSettled(uint256 roundId) external onlyKeeper;
```
**Parameters**

|Name|Type|Description|
|----|----|-----------|
|`roundId`|`uint256`|The id of the round to be settled|


### setRoundSettledBatch

Batch variant of `setRoundSettled`. Settles several rounds in one keeper transaction.

Each id must be in `InSettlement`. Restricted to the keeper role.


```solidity
function setRoundSettledBatch(uint256[] memory roundIds) external onlyKeeper;
```
**Parameters**

|Name|Type|Description|
|----|----|-----------|
|`roundIds`|`uint256[]`|The ids of the rounds to be settled|


### emergencyRollbackRound

Recovery path that moves a stuck `InSettlement` round back to `Opened` so users can
redeem their receipts via the current-round path.

Intended when `setRoundSettled` cannot proceed (e.g. underlying off-chain settlement
failed). Pairs with `retryRound` when settlement becomes possible again. Reverts if the
round is not in `InSettlement`. Restricted to the governor role.


```solidity
function emergencyRollbackRound(uint256 roundId) external onlyGovernor;
```
**Parameters**

|Name|Type|Description|
|----|----|-----------|
|`roundId`|`uint256`|The id of the round to roll back|


### _getAccessManager

Wires the inherited `Whitelist` helper to the same `ProtocolAccessManagerV2` instance
configured for `ProtocolAccessManagedV2`, so all whitelist checks flow through one
authority.


```solidity
function _getAccessManager() internal view override returns (address);
```

### validateMinPosition

Validates that both outgoing and incoming parties meet the minimum aggregate position
size, post-flight (`_;` first) so the check sees the final on-chain balances.


```solidity
modifier validateMinPosition(address outgoing, address incoming) ;
```
**Parameters**

|Name|Type|Description|
|----|----|-----------|
|`outgoing`|`address`|The address whose position is decreasing. Use `address(0)` to skip the check on that side (e.g. for deposits into an Input vault, where the depositor's position grows, no party is "outgoing"). For self-operations (`outgoing == incoming`), a full exit (zero remaining aggregate balance) is allowed.|
|`incoming`|`address`|The address whose position is increasing. Skipped if it equals `outgoing` (the self case), if it is `address(0)`, or if it is `address(this)`.|


### deposit

Deposits `assets` of the underlying token into the currently open round and mints
round-receipt tokens to `receiver`

Mints Vault shares with the given id to receiver by depositing exactly amount of underlying tokens.
- MUST emit the Deposit event.
- MAY support an additional flow in which the underlying tokens are owned by the Vault contract before the
deposit execution, and are accounted for during deposit.
- MUST revert if all of assets cannot be deposited (due to deposit limit being reached, slippage, the user not
approving enough underlying tokens to the Vault contract, etc).
NOTE: most implementations will require pre-approval of the Vault with the Vault’s underlying asset token.


```solidity
function deposit(
    uint256 assets,
    address receiver
)
    public
    virtual
    override(IERC4626MultiToken, ERC4626MultiToken)
    validateMinPosition(VAULT_TYPE == BaseVaultType.Input ? address(0) : _msgSender(), receiver)
    returns (uint256);
```
**Parameters**

|Name|Type|Description|
|----|----|-----------|
|`assets`|`uint256`|The amount of underlying tokens to deposit|
|`receiver`|`address`|The address that receives the minted shares|

**Returns**

|Name|Type|Description|
|----|----|-----------|
|`<none>`|`uint256`|shares The amount of shares minted|


### redeem

Burns exactly shares from owner and sends assets of underlying tokens to receiver.
- MUST emit the Withdraw event.
- MAY support an additional flow in which the underlying tokens are owned by the Vault contract before the
redeem execution, and are accounted for during redeem.
- MUST revert if all of shares cannot be redeemed (due to withdrawal limit being reached, slippage, the owner
not having enough shares, etc).
NOTE: some implementations will require pre-requesting to the Vault before a withdrawal may be performed.
Those methods should be performed separately.


```solidity
function redeem(
    uint256 id,
    uint256 amount,
    address receiver,
    address owner
)
    public
    virtual
    override(IERC4626MultiToken, ERC4626MultiToken)
    validateMinPosition(owner, receiver)
    returns (uint256);
```
**Parameters**

|Name|Type|Description|
|----|----|-----------|
|`id`|`uint256`|The round-receipt token id to redeem (must be the currently open round)|
|`amount`|`uint256`|The amount of round-receipt tokens to redeem|
|`receiver`|`address`|The address that receives the redeemed assets|
|`owner`|`address`|The address whose round-receipt tokens are burned|

**Returns**

|Name|Type|Description|
|----|----|-----------|
|`<none>`|`uint256`|assets The amount of underlying assets sent to the receiver|


### redeemBatch

Burns each batch of shares and the specific amounts and sends assets of underlying tokens to receiver.
- MUST emit the WithdrawBatch event.
- MAY support an additional flow in which the underlying tokens are owned by the Vault contract before the
redeem execution, and are accounted for during redeem.
- MUST revert if all of shares cannot be redeemed (due to withdrawal limit being reached, slippage, the owner
not having enough shares, etc).
NOTE: some implementations will require pre-requesting to the Vault before a withdrawal may be performed.
Those methods should be performed separately.

All `ids` must equal the currently open round. To exchange settled-round receipts for the
exchange asset, use `redeemExchangeAssetBatch` instead.


```solidity
function redeemBatch(
    uint256[] memory ids,
    uint256[] memory amounts,
    address receiver,
    address owner
)
    public
    virtual
    override(IERC4626MultiToken, ERC4626MultiToken)
    validateMinPosition(owner, receiver)
    returns (uint256 assets);
```
**Parameters**

|Name|Type|Description|
|----|----|-----------|
|`ids`|`uint256[]`|The round-receipt token ids to redeem (all must be the currently open round)|
|`amounts`|`uint256[]`|The amounts of each round-receipt token to redeem|
|`receiver`|`address`|The address that receives the redeemed assets|
|`owner`|`address`|The address whose round-receipt tokens are burned|

**Returns**

|Name|Type|Description|
|----|----|-----------|
|`assets`|`uint256`|The total amount of underlying assets sent to the receiver|


### redeemExchangeAsset

Burns receipts from a past, settled round and pays out the exchange asset at the rate
snapshotted for that round.

The exchange asset is target vault shares for `Input` flavor and the target vault's
underlying for `Output` flavor. Reverts if the round is the current open round or if the
round is not in `Settled` state. Caller must be the owner or be approved for all by the
owner. Caller, owner and receiver must all be whitelisted on the target vault context.


```solidity
function redeemExchangeAsset(
    uint256 id,
    uint256 amount,
    address receiver,
    address owner
)
    public
    validateMinPosition(owner, receiver)
    returns (uint256);
```
**Parameters**

|Name|Type|Description|
|----|----|-----------|
|`id`|`uint256`|The round id whose receipts are being burned|
|`amount`|`uint256`|The amount of receipts to burn|
|`receiver`|`address`|The address that receives the exchange asset|
|`owner`|`address`|The address whose receipts are burned, in case the caller is not the owner|

**Returns**

|Name|Type|Description|
|----|----|-----------|
|`<none>`|`uint256`|The amount of exchange asset transferred to `receiver`|


### redeemExchangeAssetBatch

Batch variant of `redeemExchangeAsset`. Burns receipts from several past settled rounds
in one call and pays out the sum of their per-round exchange amounts.

Partial redemptions are allowed, but each `(id, amount)` pair is converted using the
round's snapshotted rate and integer multiplication; redeeming a very small amount against
a sub-unit rate can therefore truncate to zero exchange asset for that line. Callers that
want exact-trade semantics should redeem each receipt in full.


```solidity
function redeemExchangeAssetBatch(
    uint256[] calldata ids,
    uint256[] calldata amounts,
    address receiver,
    address owner
)
    public
    validateMinPosition(owner, receiver)
    returns (uint256 shares);
```
**Parameters**

|Name|Type|Description|
|----|----|-----------|
|`ids`|`uint256[]`|The round ids whose receipts are being burned|
|`amounts`|`uint256[]`|The amount of receipts to burn per round id (must match `ids` length)|
|`receiver`|`address`|The address that receives the exchange asset|
|`owner`|`address`|The address whose receipts are burned, in case the caller is not the owner|

**Returns**

|Name|Type|Description|
|----|----|-----------|
|`shares`|`uint256`|(legacy name) — total amount of *exchange asset* transferred to `receiver`. For the `Input` flavor this is target-vault shares; for the `Output` flavor this is the target vault's underlying asset. The parameter is named `shares` for historical reasons and is not always denominated in vault shares.|

### exchangeAsset

Returns the ERC-20 token paid out when exchanging a settled-round receipt.

For `Input` vaults this is the target vault's share token; for `Output` vaults this is
the target vault's underlying asset.


```solidity
function exchangeAsset() public view override returns (address);
```
**Returns**

|Name|Type|Description|

### setMinPositionSize

Sets the minimum aggregate position size that a user must maintain to enter or exit.

Setting `0` disables the check. The minimum is denominated in target-vault assets and is
evaluated post-flight against the user's combined receipt + target-vault-share balance.
Restricted to the governor role.


```solidity
function setMinPositionSize(uint256 minSize) external override onlyGovernor;
```
**Parameters**

|Name|Type|Description|
|----|----|-----------|
|`minSize`|`uint256`|The new minimum position size, or 0 to disable|


### getExchangeRate

Returns the per-round exchange rate snapshotted when the round was settled.

The rate is stored as a `Price{ baseAmount, quoteAmount }` where `baseAmount` is the total
exchange-asset amount produced by the settlement trade and `quoteAmount` is the total
deposit-asset amount that was frozen for the round. `PriceUtils.quote(rate, amount)`
converts a receipt amount into the matching exchange-asset amount. Returns a zero-valued
`Price` for rounds that have not been settled yet.


```solidity
function getExchangeRate(uint256 round) public view returns (Price memory);
```
**Parameters**

|Name|Type|Description|
|----|----|-----------|
|`round`|`uint256`|The round id to look up|

**Returns**

|Name|Type|Description|
|----|----|-----------|
|`<none>`|`Price`|The `Price{ baseAmount, quoteAmount }` snapshot for `round`, or a zero-valued `Price` if the round has not been settled.|


### _validateAggregateAssets

Reverts with `RoundsVaultPositionTooSmall` if the user's aggregate post-flight position
is non-zero but below `_minPositionSize`. For Input flavor, open receipts are counted
1:1 as assets (they represent capital queued to be deposited); for Output flavor receipts
are treated as 0 (they represent capital already on the way out). Both flavors additionally
count any target-vault shares the user holds, converted to assets via `convertToAssets`.


```solidity
function _validateAggregateAssets(
    address user,
    bool isInputVault,
    uint256 _minPositionSize,
    address targetVault
)
    internal
    view;
```
**Parameters**

|Name|Type|Description|
|----|----|-----------|
|`user`|`address`|The address being evaluated|
|`isInputVault`|`bool`|`true` for Input flavor, `false` for Output flavor|
|`_minPositionSize`|`uint256`|The minimum aggregate position size, in target-vault assets|
|`targetVault`|`address`|The target ERC-4626 vault address|


### _startSettlement

Helper that moves an `Opened` round to `InSettlement`. Used both by `nextRound`
(closing the current round) and `retryRound` (re-attempting a previously rolled-back
past round).


```solidity
function _startSettlement(uint256 roundId) internal;
```
**Parameters**

|Name|Type|Description|
|----|----|-----------|
|`roundId`|`uint256`|The id of the round to transition|


### _getMintId

Returns the Id to be used for minting the receipt

This function must be overridden by the child contract to implement any desired strategy


```solidity
function _getMintId() internal view virtual override returns (uint256);
```

### _operate

Settlement hook: executes the actual deposit-into or redeem-from the target vault for
a round's frozen liability.

Implementations are expected to call `_depositOnTarget` (Input flavor) or
`_redeemFromTarget` (Output flavor) and return the exact amount the target vault paid
back, so the caller can snapshot the per-round exchange rate from real execution.


```solidity
function _operate(uint256 amount, uint256 roundId) internal virtual returns (uint256 outputAmount);
```
**Parameters**

|Name|Type|Description|
|----|----|-----------|
|`amount`|`uint256`|The exact amount frozen for the round (deposit asset for Input, shares for Output)|
|`roundId`|`uint256`|The id of the round being settled|

**Returns**

|Name|Type|Description|
|----|----|-----------|
|`outputAmount`|`uint256`|The exact amount the target vault returned after the settlement trade|


### _getFallbackExchangeRate

Returns the exchange rate used when a round had no deposits at settlement time.

Implementations typically derive the rate from the target vault's `previewDeposit`
(Input) or `previewRedeem` (Output) so empty rounds still snapshot a sensible price.


```solidity
function _getFallbackExchangeRate() internal view virtual returns (Price memory);
```

### _setRoundSettled

Helper that runs the actual settlement: flips the round state to `Settled` first
(so any reentry sees a terminal state), then calls `_operate` against the frozen
total supply, and finally snapshots the per-round exchange rate from the real result.
Empty rounds (no receipts minted) fall back to `_getFallbackExchangeRate()`.

Reverts unless `roundState[roundId] == InSettlement`.


```solidity
function _setRoundSettled(uint256 roundId) internal;
```
**Parameters**

|Name|Type|Description|
|----|----|-----------|
|`roundId`|`uint256`|The id of the round to settle|


### _redeemExchangeAsset

Burns receipts for a settled round and pays out the matching exchange-asset amount.

Caller authorization (must be the owner or an operator approved by the owner) is checked
here; round-state and id-validity checks live in the public entry point. Follows CEI:
burn first, compute the payout, then transfer — the ERC-1155 `_burn` debits the owner's
balance up front so a reentrant `tokensReceived` (ERC-777) callback on `safeTransfer`
cannot drain.


```solidity
function _redeemExchangeAsset(
    address caller,
    address receiver,
    address owner,
    uint256 id,
    uint256 amount
)
    private
    returns (uint256 exchangeAmount);
```
**Parameters**

|Name|Type|Description|
|----|----|-----------|
|`caller`|`address`|The address that invoked the redemption|
|`receiver`|`address`|The address that receives the exchange asset|
|`owner`|`address`|The address whose receipts are burned|
|`id`|`uint256`|The round id being exchanged|
|`amount`|`uint256`|The number of receipts to burn|

**Returns**

|Name|Type|Description|
|----|----|-----------|
|`exchangeAmount`|`uint256`|The amount of exchange asset paid to `receiver`|


### _redeemExchangeAssetBatch

Batch variant of `_redeemExchangeAsset`. Burns receipts for several settled rounds in
one call and pays out the cumulative exchange-asset amount.

Caller authorization is checked here; round-state and id-validity checks live in the
public entry point. Follows the same CEI ordering as `_redeemExchangeAsset` — the batch
burn debits owner balances before the single trailing `safeTransfer`.


```solidity
function _redeemExchangeAssetBatch(
    address caller,
    address receiver,
    address owner,
    uint256[] memory ids,
    uint256[] memory amounts
)
    private
    returns (uint256 exchangeAmount);
```
**Parameters**

|Name|Type|Description|
|----|----|-----------|
|`caller`|`address`|The address that invoked the redemption|
|`receiver`|`address`|The address that receives the exchange asset|
|`owner`|`address`|The address whose receipts are burned|
|`ids`|`uint256[]`|The round ids being exchanged|
|`amounts`|`uint256[]`|The receipts burned per round id (aligned with `ids`)|

**Returns**

|Name|Type|Description|
|----|----|-----------|
|`exchangeAmount`|`uint256`|The total exchange asset paid to `receiver`|
